senses.gloss:
Su-varṇa, ‘beautiful coloured,’ is an epithet of gold (Hiraṇya),
and then comes to be used as a substantive denoting ‘gold.’
^1) Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa, i. 4, 7, 4;
8, 9, 1, etc.
^2) Av. xv. 1, 2; Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa,
iii. 12, 6, 6; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, xi. 4,
1, 8, etc.; Chāndogya Upaniṣad, i. 6, 6;
iii. 19, 1; iv. 17, 7, etc.

Su-vasana in the Rigveda denotes a ‘splendid garment,’^1
and is also used adjectivally, ‘clothing well.’^2 Su-vāsas, ‘well-
dressed,’ is a common adjective.^3 See Vāsas.
1) vi. 51, 4.
2) ix. 97, 50.
3) Rv. i. 124, 7; iii. 8, 4; x. 71, 4, etc.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 262.

Su-vāstu (‘having fair dwellings’) is the name of a river in the
Rigveda.^1 It is clearly the Soastos of Arrian^2 and the modern
Swāt, a tributary of the Kubhā (Kabul river) which is itself an
affluent of the Indus.
1) viii. 19, 37; Nirukta, iv. 15.
2) Indica, iv. 11.
Cf. Roth, Nirukta, Erlänterungen, 43;
Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 18; Ludwig,
Translation of the Rigveda, 3. 200;
Imperial Gazetteer of India, 23, 187.
